sketches.title: Barnyard Chain Reaction
sketches.premise: The farmyard is having a bad day, and each player adds one standing farmyard thing that causes the last thing to fail. A chicken can scatter grain, a fox can catch a chicken, and a farmer can chase a fox; keep the trouble moving until someone proposes a cause that does not actually beat what stands.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that your new thing directly acts on and defeats the previous thing by a plain farmyard cause; merely avoiding it, lasting through it, making a bigger copy, or naming a related thing without an action loses.
sketches.move_shape: Say what you are and the simple trouble you cause: "I am a muddy boot; I squash the worm." Host: "The worm has met footwear and lost its dignity."

sketches.title: Field Tool Lock
sketches.premise: Two players build a farm job one tool at a time. Your tool must stop, undo, or make useless the job done by the tool before it, so the chain jumps from shovel to hose to wheelbarrow to gate and onward.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the named tool plainly defeats the previous tool's current farm job by blocking, undoing, or taking over its work; hiding from it, merely being stronger, or offering a similar tool without a counter loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name a tool and its direct answer: "I am a rake; I pull apart the pile the shovel made." Host: "A tidy rebuttal, though the rake is asking for a promotion."

sketches.title: Animal Job Swap
sketches.premise: Each turn brings in a farm animal whose natural job ruins the job of the animal before it. A cow tramples a nest, a dog herds the cow, and a cat scares the dog; animals win through what they plainly do, not through heroic imagination.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new animal uses an ordinary behavior to stop or spoil the previous animal's standing action; escape, endurance, a larger version of the same animal, and a vague family resemblance do not count.
sketches.move_shape: Say the animal and its job: "I am a goose; I chase the dog away from the feed." Host: "The goose has selected violence, or at least loud paperwork."

sketches.title: Weather on the Farm
sketches.premise: The sky over the farm changes by direct consequence. Each player names one weather condition that beats the last by stopping it, undoing it, or changing what it can do: rain beats dust, sun beats frost, and wind can scatter smoke.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new weather directly cancels or changes the previous weather's effect; merely surviving it, slipping around it, making it bigger, or using a poetic cousin of it loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name the weather and its effect: "I am rain; I pin the dust to the road." Host: "The dust has been grounded for being too dramatic."

sketches.title: Farm Fence Fight
sketches.premise: The farm's boundaries keep changing as players add one standing obstacle or solution that defeats the last one. A fence blocks a cow, wire cutters defeat the fence, a locked shed defeats the cutters, and a key defeats the lock.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new object plainly blocks, breaks, opens, traps, or otherwise defeats the previous object's function; walking around it, outlasting it, using a bigger copy, or naming a nearby object without a mechanism loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name the object and what it does: "I am a gate; I stop the cow from reaching the cabbage." Host: "The cabbage receives a brief legal victory."

sketches.title: Barnyard Sound-Off
sketches.premise: The farm is making one noise at a time, and each player introduces a standing farmyard thing that shuts down or defeats the noise before it. A rooster's crow meets earmuffs, earmuffs meet a whistle, and a closed barn can stop the whistle from getting out.
sketches.criterion: The Judge checks that the new thing directly muffles, interrupts, traps, or otherwise stops the previous sound; ignoring it, being louder, surviving the noise, or offering a related sound without a stopping mechanism loses.
sketches.move_shape: Name the thing and its sound-stopping action: "I am a blanket; I smother the drumbeat." Host: "The drum has been tucked in. Its concert career is over."
